HRA Analysis: STOLEN ONE (1) gets the advantage from the pole draw after two super-impressive victories in handy time throughout the Sweepstakes series. She takes on the boys here, but with the draw advantage she looks the horse to beat. HAVEYOUMETMAYNARD (3) was good first up from a break after doing some work early and still running a slick last half before being run down late by a handy one. Tactics will be interesting here, but his class should take him a long way and give the expected favourite a run for her money. OUR ROB ROY (2) has also shown good ability thus far in his career and should be suited settling closer along the pegs. He showed a brilliant turn of foot two starts back, producing a very fast quarter to nearly win, and will be looking to do something similar here. SOLO STITCH (4) is the most experienced runner in the field and continues to produce competitive performances, but may lack the class of some of his rivals here, especially from the widest draw where he is likely to settle last. Selections:STOLEN ONE (1), HAVEYOUMETMAYNARD (3), OUR ROB ROY (2), SOLO STITCH (4)

The standing-start event sees brilliant beginner ALBERIO (2) likely to ping away and be first to the pegs, where he will have options from there. He looks to get his chance to finish on the podium after racing somewhat below his best over the past few months. SPORTZSILK (1) attempts the stand for the first time, and his first-up run for the new stable last week was good enough to see him in the finish here if he steps cleanly. REPETITIVE (4) is normally a good beginner and went close to winning last start when second against a similar field, so should be thereabouts again. SAPPHIRE GAMBLER (6) returned to the winner's circle last week when making a mid-race move and proving far too strong. Similar tactics may be adopted again here, which would make him one of the hardest to beat. The 20-metre runners WE SALUTE YOU (7) and JOHN VINCENT (8) are clearly the class horses of the field and have been racing competitively in stronger company than they meet here. It's always difficult to make up ground over the middle-distance standing start, but their class should take them a long way. Selections:SAPPHIRE GAMBLER (6), WE SALUTE YOU (7), JOHN VINCENT (8), SPORTZSILK (1)

RESURGENT WARRIOR (2) should be able to cross to the pegs and lead over the short distance, which should give him his best chance of winning. SHADES OF SILK (3) looks likely to again have to do the hard yards outside the leader, but has battled on gamely in good time at his past few starts and should do the same again here. JET TO HEAVEN (1) again draws the pole and should get every chance along the pegs late. JUST LIKA DREAM (4) and LADY IN LINE (5) may have to be driven with a sit and will be relying on genuine tempo and a nice run into the race to be finishing home strongly, as will GOBSMACKED (7), who draws the outside gate but rattled home to win last start. KENYA (8) draws his worst possible gate, with his best racing normally coming when driven hard on speed. He may be forced to stay three pegs here and hope for an even tempo, but if the gaps appear late, he will be right in the finish. Selections:RESURGENT WARRIOR (2), SHADES OF SILK (3), KENYA (8), JET TO HEAVEN (1)

TALK IS CHEAP (7) was a tough winner last start after copping pressure early when leading and still proving too strong by over nine metres late. She draws a wide gate here and rises slightly in class, but would only need to reproduce that effort to be right in the finish again. REALLY SMARTIE (5) is an eight-year-old gelding making his first start for Team McKenzie after arriving from Victoria. He has mixed his form over time but clearly possesses the ability to be in the finish if he can produce something near his best. Another runner making their state debut is OUR DANCE MONKEY (1), who competed in strong races as a younger horse and has been competitive against better classed horses than she meets here. She is aided by the pole draw and looks a good chance to break through for the new stable off her latest trial effort. DENVER MAN (9) returns to the state, where his most recent victory came last October. He has been misbehaving of late, but if he brings his best manners, he should be running home strongly from the nice trailing draw. DOLCE DRAMA (4) was well backed when second last start and, with another nice run in transit, should be finishing home strongly again. BUSLOAD OF FAITH (6) produced an improved effort last start when sitting outside the leader over the short distance and will no doubt again look to roll forward from his draw, although he does have a tendency to over-race. At his best, he is certainly good enough to take this out. Selections:OUR DANCE MONKEY (1), DOLCE DRAMA (4), TALK IS CHEAP (7), REALLY SMARTIE (5)

Another strong No More Than Two Lifetime Wins event, where they compete over the mile after running very solid time over the middle distance last start. REMMINGTON (4) made a mid-race move last start and toughed it out well when fourth, and should get his chance on speed again here to be in the finish. BEARHUNTA (6) is first up in the state for visiting trainer Dean Braun and has built a handy record in his short career, despite now being a five-year-old. He strikes a tricky draw over the short distance, so it will be interesting to see how confidently they drive him from the gate, as he may be caught wide early if they push forward, but his class could still prevail. ULTIMATE GLADIATOR(8) was good first up in the state after arriving from the Riverina. He draws awkwardly on the inside of the back row, but if the gaps appear, he should again be finishing home strongly. MAXX (11) and SOHO TIGERLILY (12) have been consistent since arriving in the state but may require those up front to overdo it to bring them into the race over the short distance. TWILIGHT STORM (5) recently ran second in the Oaks and expect she may roll forward from the middle front-row draw to give herself her best chance. A ROCKN NIGHTMARE (3) is another making her first start in the state and should look to find a position on speed with cover. Selections:BEARHUNTA (6), TWILIGHT STORM (5), REMMINGTON (4), ULTIMATE GLADIATOR (8)

VIVID DREAM (2) was ultra impressive first up in the state, making a dashing run from back in the field off a slippery last half and proving far too good. He takes on the older horses here but clearly looks the one to beat. I GOTTA GO (1) again draws a favourable gate after setting a hot tempo in the above race and only being beaten 10 metres. He has the gate speed to find a forward position and have options thereafter, giving him every chance to finish on the podium again. IDEN OLIVER (6) is chasing four straight victories and is putting together a very impressive record when combining with claiming driver Grace Jones. He strikes an awkward gate, but it wouldn't surprise to see them roll forward in a front row that isn't overly blessed with gate speed to give him his best chance. SHOOBEES SPIRIT (11) and MOVESLIKEALADY (12) will again be driven for their sit-sprint capabilities and should be finishing off strongly. However, there doesn't appear to be a lot of pressure up front to ensure a genuine tempo through the middle stages, which may make their task more difficult. MISS COLLANN (8) again gets her chance to improve from the nice inside back-row draw and should get every opportunity to run into a placing. Selections:VIVID DREAM (2), I GOTTA GO (1), MISS COLLANN (8), IDEN OLIVER (6)

An even field combines for the low-class race of the night, where KYRGIOS (4) produced a handy second first up for the new stable and should be further improved from that run. Expect him to settle somewhere around midfield in a front row that is blessed with plenty of gate speed from all angles when asked. PARK LANE (6) should be first to the pegs if on his best manners and could be the one at odds if he settles in running. FEELINKINDALUCKY (5) received a nice run in transit to return to the winner's circle last start. He draws awkwardly here but, with another favourable run in transit, should be right in the finish. ROSE NOIRE (7), STAROFREMEMBRANCE (8) and QUEENOFDANCE (9) are always capable of running home strongly in races of this nature. With the expected hot tempo early and KIAVINO STRIDE (10) likely to keep the speed on through the middle stages, they should get their chance to finish over the top with the right runs. Selections:KYRGIOS (4), ROSE NOIRE (7), QUEENOFDANCE (9), STAROFREMEMBRANCE (8)

A competitive 70 to 79 NR event sees EVERYTHING BUT THE (1) looking to continue his winning ways after two impressive victories of late. Expect he may again cop some early pressure from those drawn outside him, but with any luck in running, he should again be right in the finish from the nice pole draw. RAY DAN (2) resumes from a break after three handy trials and showed what he is capable of with some strong performances before heading out for a spell. He should get a nice sit on speed with cover and will be hard to hold out if fit enough. WAZZA (4) is in a similar boat being first up and draws a middle-of-the-road gate, but has a handy record overall and looks a genuine danger. GOODTIME OSCAR (3) is a tough customer and again draws nicely to find a position on speed and be battling it out over the final furlong. It wouldn't surprise to see any of the others in this field bob up if the race is run at a solid tempo, including ANOTHER NIEN (6), who is always capable of running home strongly. VANQUISH STRIDE (8), the lone runner off the back row, may be driven for a soft run along the pegs and should be finishing home strongly if the gaps appear late. Selections:EVERYTHING BUT THE (1), RAY DAN (2), GOODTIME OSCAR (3), WAZZA (4)

The open-class handicap is over the longer distance, where CUSTOM HARLEY (5) should be extremely well suited by the trip. He's a tough customer and was good when making late ground in fast time last start, and will no doubt be out there looking to out-tough his rivals again. WAVES OF CHANCE (6) returned to form when dropping back in grade over his preferred mile trip last start. He galloped away badly at his first attempt from the standing start, but may be better suited following horses out from the 10-metre handicap here. If he can settle in running, he possesses the speed to sprint home strongly late in the small field. The trio off the front row, WATERMELON SUGAR (1), IRON CLAD (2) and KEAYANG FITZY (3), continue to earn cheques for connections in this class of race without breaking through, but again get their chance with the advantage of starting off the front. POWER UP (4) is another who will need to begin better from the stand than he has in the past, but could be the one at odds finishing home strongly if he brings his best. ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (7) can't be left out and, like the expected favourite CUSTOM HARLEY (5), should be very well suited by the longer distance and standing-start conditions. He should be kicking on strongly over the final stages. Selections:CUSTOM HARLEY (5), ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (7), WAVES OF CHANCE (6), WATERMELON SUGAR (1)

A small field comes together for the final race of the day over the sprint trip, with numerous runners possessing good gate speed. LYNRYD SKYNRYD (4) looks likely to be first to the pegs and was good when third in fast time over the same journey last start. He should again run a cheeky race at odds. MISTA EAGLE (5) can also fly the gate when asked, but expect he may be driven with a sit here, knowing he is unlikely to cross his stablemate mentioned above. LAID BACK (2) showed terrific gate speed from out wide a few starts back and was only run down in good time. He draws nicely here to be right in the finish and is certainly due to break through. DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (1) continues to race consistently and should enjoy a solid tempo throughout, allowing him to finish home strongly if the gaps appear late. WILL HE PIKE (3) returns to the mobile after racing well from handicaps in standing-start events at his past few starts. While he also possesses very sharp gate speed when asked, expect he may be driven with a sit here in the hope of out dashing them late. MONTGOMERY BURNS (6) may need to improve on recent efforts to be in the finish but should still get his chance in the small field. Selections:WILL HE PIKE (3), DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (1), LAID BACK (2), LYNRYD SKYNRYD (4) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW: This opening event is an even field with many winning chances. DALLASCOWBOY (9) was well beaten two starts ago, but it was a heat of the Vicbred Super Series won by the talented The Niteshift. Last start, he was only beaten 7.7 metres in a fast 1.51.9 mile rate at Wagga. He’s only lightly raced and he’s racing better than his numerical form suggests. CHAINSMOKE (6) returned a winner last start at Swan Hill after 10 months on the sidelines. He flashed home powerfully in the run. This race is harder, but he will have improved with fitness. ASSIGNED (3) was retired out of the race last start with a flat tyre. He was first up in two months on that occasion. He has ability and will likely map in the running line here before running home late. OWEN THE SAINTS (8) has a great turn of foot and will be flashing home with clear running late. An interesting runner to note here is TA KALCHE (5). He’s an eight-year-old gelding having his second career start and hasn’t raced in 792 days. BACK: DALLASCOWBOY (9) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:DALLASCOWBOY (9), CHAINSMOKE (6), ASSIGNED (3), OWEN THE SAINTS (8)

OVERVIEW: This is a field full of talented and progressive horses. ATUA MAGIC (2) is a very smart horse whose talent we have only seen glimpses of in his short career. He is having his third start this year and his first run this year over the shorter trip. If he is able to get forward, he will be hard to beat if he brings his best. JACCKA EVAN (9) is an ex-New Zealand horse who made his Australian debut earlier this month at Wagga. He worked forward to the front there and was too good. He will improve with fitness here. FOURTH RESPONSE (4) made a run from last last start at Melton to finish third behind Hitch To His Star and Lougle. He is racing well. The race map could be awkward for him here. FOLLOWTHEACE (7), KOSIMO (5), MITZI SAID (6) and ROYAL APPOINTMENT (8) will be needing luck here, but they are capable. BACK: ATUA MAGIC (2) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:ATUA MAGIC (2), JACCKA EVAN (9), FOURTH RESPONSE (4), FOLLOWTHEACE (7)

OVERVIEW: TEERDEE (6) was impressive last start in the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series Final won by Kahula. She finished fifth but had no clear running late and was hitting the line impressively. Barrier six is awkward as she lacks gate speed. The horse drawn inside her, SPUN SILVER (5), has brilliant gate speed. NINEDOLLA TOASTIE (9) had to work hard early last start at Geelong, leaving her vulnerable late to swoopers. But she was only beaten 9.1 metres and battled on well. Prior to that, she was consistently running well. FOUR EVER A STAR (4) is a horse I am expecting to see improvement from here. She has had two starts this month after three years on the sidelines. She would have needed those runs for fitness. THERESHEWAS (8) has a nice turn of foot when saved for one run. If she gets splits late, she may be running home well. BACK: TEERDEE (6) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:TEERDEE (6), NINEDOLLA TOASTIE (9), FOUR EVER A STAR (4), THERESHEWAS (8)

OVERVIEW: This looks like another even contest where a case can be made for many runners. MIKI MARK (5) was stuck in the breeze last start at Cranbourne but battled on well for fourth. He’s been racing well, he’s just had a bit of bad luck. If he can overcome barrier five, he finds a suitable race to get back into the winner’s circle. GLENLINE (4) was eye-catching last start. He was last at the top of the straight but flashed home well for second. He often gets back in his runs and relies on his powerful finishing burst. CINQUANTA (3)’s last three runs have been improved and she looks like she’s ready to get back into the winner’s circle. If she can get into a forward position and have a good trip throughout, she will be a big threat. ZU HOFFEN (6) and KUTANI (7) are winning chances at their best, but they are early into their preparations and fitness could be an issue. Also respecting TREACHEROUSTIMES (8) and QUEENHIGH FLUSH (9) as winning chances. SELECTIONS:MIKI MARK (5), GLENLINE (4), CINQUANTA (3), ZU HOFFEN (6)

OVERVIEW: KYVALLEY MISTY (9) had issues with her manners early in her career, but she does seem to be figuring it out now. Her three runs this preparation have been strong and if she does everything right here, she will be hard to beat. FLING IT RAINBOW (5) is a trotter who can run home nicely when saved for one run. If he can slot in somewhere and not do much work early, he’s a threat in this. CHARLIE WALKER (3) was below his best last start when dropping out late at Maryborough. His run prior to that was strong at Ballarat when he led and won. If he brings his best, he is in this. MAJOR MAX (2) has the barrier to capitalise on here if he does everything right. He is racing well when he trots throughout. BACK: KYVALLEY MISTY (9) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:KYVALLEY MISTY (9), FLING IT RAINBOW (5), CHARLIE WALKER (3), MAJOR MAX (2)

OVERVIEW: BET BET HOTSHOT (3)’s numerical form isn’t fantastic, but she has the best sectional times in this event and she has the gate speed to map positively here. BETSY ANNE (4) looks ready to get back into the winner’s circle. She was second last start at Swan Hill when getting an ideal fence trip. With luck here, this is a winnable race for her. PLAYA DEL CARMEN (2) and NUCLEAR ATTITUDE (8) are racing OK and can capitalise on good barriers here to have options. SELECTIONS:BET BET HOTSHOT (3), BETSY ANNE (4), PLAYA DEL CARMEN (2), NUCLEAR ATTITUDE (8)

OVERVIEW: LORD LOGAN (6) has only had the four career starts, for three ultra-impressive victories. The only time he has been beaten was when he paced under pressure in a tougher race than this one. He is still learning, but he’s progressive and exciting. KITTY CASH (5) was just too good winning last start at Cranbourne after racing in the breeze. She is a smart mare when she does everything right. I AM HARRO (4) is a nice trotter at his best, and he’s currently racing well. DEEJAY DEX (7) often gets back at the start of his races and flashes home well late. He’s likely to do the same here, but there will be talent in front of him that he will be chasing. BACK: LORD LOGAN (6) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:LORD LOGAN (6), KITTY CASH (5), I AM HARRO (4), DEEJAY DEX (7)

OVERVIEW: FLYIN TIME (3) is consistently running well each start this campaign, not finishing worse than fourth in her last five starts. With luck here, she’s a winning chance. LOVE ME AGAIN (1) turned his form around with a win last start at this track when finding late runs through the field. He gets a good barrier to be competitive again. ALDEBARAN DENBAY (4) also got back into the winner’s circle last start, flashing home to defeat FLYIN TIME (3) last start. He can get it wrong with his manners, so if he can settle, he is right in this again. THE CHOOK (5) has been getting back and flashing home recently in his runs. Barrier five is sticky. SELECTIONS:FLYIN TIME (3), LOVE ME AGAIN (1), ALDEBARAN DENBAY (4), THE CHOOK (5)

OVERVIEW: CHAMPAGNES (6) got well back last start but ran home well into fourth. She’s been in career-best form recently and finds a good race here. STRAIGHT TO THETOP (5) was good hitting the line into second two starts ago after being back on the fence. Last start, she tired when leading in an arguably harder race. If she can find a comfortable trip here, she should be flashing home well late. KIMBERLEYS TREE (4) is a trotter you need to take on trust. When she is at her best and trotting safely, she races well. She can get it wrong, however. CONSTANT (3) is a consistent trotter with a nice turn of foot. With a good trip here, she is a winning chance. CHANTILLY LASS (7) is a winning chance, but manners can be an issue. SELECTIONS:CHAMPAGNES (6), STRAIGHT TO THETOP (5), KIMBERLEYS TREE (4), CONSTANT (3) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW: It is an open race to commence the afternoon and luck in running might be the key to the result. RED HOT MIKI (1) is perfectly drawn to suit his racing pattern and he had no luck last week when he was held up for a run at a vital stage so he rates as a value hope. HALF PRICE BRIDE (5) has been racing against stronger opposition in the South-East and is worth thought at her Mildura debut. Her third placed effort behind Midnight Alibi in a mile rate of 1.55.7 at Bendigo in June is a good form pointer for this event. FLAME BLASTER (6) is poorly drawn but he has returned to form recently and he didn’t have much room in the straight at his latest third. He is a winning chance if he has normal luck in running. ACCELERE (3) is rising in class but he possesses early speed and he led throughout last week so he is not without a chance. STARVIN MARVIN (7) will appreciate a drop back in class and is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: RED HOT MIKI (1), HALF PRICE BRIDE (5), FLAME BLASTER (6), ACCELERE (3)

OVERVIEW:DREAMTIME NALA (2) joins trainer Allan MacDonald after her Mildura debut second behind DIAMOND KRUSHER (1), where she raced on the outside of the leader for the majority of the trip and went down fighting. She is ideally drawn and looms as one of the leading chances again. PUNTO CALIENTE (7) settled down at the tail of the field and was the widest runner turning for home when he produced a big finish for second behind Fleur Bella last week. He is awkwardly drawn but is ready to break through for a win. SUNSHINE WARRIOR (5) has returned to his peak form over the past two weeks with a runaway victory two weeks ago followed by a third behind Accelere last week, where he was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off well. This is a race of similar standard and he is worth thought again. DIAMOND KRUSHER (1) tends to perform best over the sprint distance but she led throughout against similar grade two weeks ago and is perfectly drawn to give another forward showing. SELECTIONS: DREAMTIME NALA (2), PUNTO CALIENTE (7), SUNSHINE WARRIOR (5), DIAMOND KRUSHER (1)

OVERVIEW: OZZIE TART (3) is a juvenile filly taking on some very handy and experienced performers but she is racing well enough to get the job done. She showed exceptional gate speed in both a heat and a semi-final of the Super Series then drew on the inside of the second line when a creditable fifth in the Final at Group 1 level. VINNY ROCK (6) appears to be very well graded in this event and is the logical danger. He raced without cover throughout and battled on strongly for second behind She’s Poppy at Mildura last outing. CARLISLE CRUISER (7) hasn’t produced his best form this preparation but he will appreciate a drop back in class for this assignment and gets his chance to improve. SHIRLEY NOT (5) has been racing consistently in both Victoria and in South Australia and is capable of filling a place despite the tricky draw. SELECTIONS: OZZIE TART (3), VINNY ROCK (6), CARLISLE CRUISER (7), SHIRLEY NOT (5)

OVERVIEW: CELESTIAL NEBULAE (8) sprinted fast from a long way back when an eye-catching second behind Listen To The Hand (won again since) at Mildura last outing. He was an impressive winner at his previous two attempts and he should prove hard to beat again. BERSAGLIERE (5) was resuming since November when a game second at Gawler then followed with a fourth behind CESLESTIAL NEBULAE (8). He should be building on his fitness and has the early speed to be prominent throughout. PRIDDY CARSON (7) gained a nice trail and finished off solidly when second behind Watch The Attitude last week. He is awkwardly drawn but he should be finishing off strongly. COME ON BILLEE (4) hasn’t been able to produce his best form at Mildura with only one placed effort from six attempts to date but he won nicely at Gawler two starts ago so he cannot be left out of calculations. BACK: CELESTIAL NEBULAE (8) – 4 units (win) SELECTIONS: CELESTIAL NEBULAE (8), BERSAGLIERE (5), PRIDDY CARSON (7), COME ON BILLEE (4)

OVERVIEW:KEAYANG CRIPPA (1) gave the leaders a big start, came out three horses wide at the bell and continued to make ground when a handy third behind Fleur Bella last week. He has been racing in good form against similar opposition and will appreciate his best draw for a long time so he should prove hard to beat. OZZIE DIAMOND (7) competed in a heat of the Super Series last outing and ran a reasonable race for fifth behind the quality filly Ideal Frankie at Melton. She has the perfect trailing draw behind the likely leader in KEAYANG CRIPPA (1) so she should go well. HESASTAR (3) is a fast beginner and is usually competitive against this class. He raced without cover throughout when third behind Our Master Play at Mildura on August 28. CHALKNCHEDDAR (5) defeated a field of similar quality at Mildura three starts ago and didn’t have much luck from a wide draw at Swan Hill last outing. He is worth a ticket each way under these conditions. BACK: KEAYANG CRIPPA (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: KEAYANG CRIPPA (1), OZZIE DIAMOND (7), HESASTAR (3), CHALKNCHEDDAR (5)

OVERVIEW:NOT VICIOUS (5) is a first starter for South Australian trainer Peter Bain, which has been performing well at the trials and was a runaway winner at her latest Gawler performance in reasonable time so she is likely to be strongly fancied for her debut. MYDEEPESTDESIRE (8) appears to be the logical danger. She was caught wide early, pushed forward to race without cover at the 1300m and went down fighting when a brave and narrow second at Ballarat on debut. SWEET LUCY LOU (2) produced a big performance when fourth last week, where she raced without cover and was extremely fierce during the middle stages before battling on well for fourth. She is racing well enough to break her Maiden status in the near future. ALMIGHTY RUSH (3) was driven aggressively to find the lead and copped some pressure mid-race when a game second last week. She has claims along with LIKE A LIBRARIAN (10), which has finished nicely in two runs since resuming. SELECTIONS: NOT VICIOUS (5), MYDEEPESTDESIRE (8), SWEET LUCY LOU (2), ALMIGHTY RUSH (3)

OVERVIEW: SANTA CASA BEACH (2) was severely checked on the home turn and lost his chance when resuming since June. All of his best performances have been when he is able to lead so he is perfectly drawn to suit his racing pattern and an improved effort is expected. HOT DEAL (7) was caught wide early and was forced to restrain to a rearward position so he had little luck at his latest fifth. He boasts a strong record at Mildura and is versatile so he must be included amongst the leading chances. MAXY WANTS TO PLAY (6) ran a game race for second behind Forty Love at Mildura three starts ago then followed with a fourth at Terang. He was in a reasonable position and was severely checked on the home turn at Swan Hill last time out so he is worth another chance. The Julie Douglas trained pair OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (4) and EARL OF PEMBROKE (5) have had a few chances recently but they are dropping back in class and appear to be better placed under these conditions. BACK: SANTA CASA BEACH (2) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: SANTA CASA BEACH (2), HOT DEAL (7), MAXY WANTS TO PLAY (6), OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (4)

OVERVIEW: GOOD BOOTS BINDI (3) continues to race well against strong opposition and deserves to break through for a win. He finished off nicely from midfield when second behind Sportsbou in a slick mile rate of 1.58.5 at Mildura last outing. DON CRUNCH (2) was driven aggressively to find the lead and remained strong at the finish when a comfortable winner at Mildura last outing. He is a lightly raced gelding with ability and should be competitive again. SHES POPPY (1) led throughout over the sprint distant two weeks ago then surrendered the lead over the longer trip and finished second to CHEERS POVERTY (8) last week. She should receive every chance from the pole position and is one of the leading chances again. LETSGO BIG GIRL (11) attempted to lead throughout when third behind Bizzness Class last week. She is a short course specialist so the drop back in distance is an advantage and she should be finishing off well. BACK: GOOD BOOTS BINDI (3) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: GOOD BOOTS BINDI (3), DON CRUNCH (2), SHES POPPY (1), LETSGO BIG GIRL (11)

OVERVIEW: SHEER ME (3) has joined the Alex Ashwood stable following a couple of really encouraging runs and looks well placed to break her maiden in the opening event of the night. Last time at Kilmore, she worked to find the front and got little peace, but still boxed on extremely well to run third. Before that at Shepparton, she was trapped parked and only beaten 4.2m into third in a slick enough last half of 56.9. This looks very suitable and keen she goes close. KAIDENBOY (2) has had just the three starts and hasn’t been beaten far in two of them so is a definite danger, RETRO FIT (1) draws well and produced a career best fourth last time at Cranbourne behind a smart one in Twigstar, while THE FEENY FAVOURITE (6) and WHIRLY MAURZ (4) have had plenty of goes but are probably next best. BACK: SHEER ME (3) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: SHEER ME (3), KAIDENBOY (2), RETRO FIT (1), THE FEENY FAVOURITE (6)

OVERVIEW: Great battle between the Michael Stanley and Emma Stewart stables here, with SOHO TRUMP (1) favoured for the former. He won the Group 2 Vicbred Super Series final as a two-year-old in 2025 and sadly missed this year’s decider after a torrid run in the semi-finals. He was trapped parked there on a hot speed and dropped out late to finish ninth. He led and won a heat at Kilmore prior to that and looks the horse to beat after the kind barrier draw as he is expected to lead. Stewart’s SEASIDE BOY (4) ran well from a bad draw in his Vicbred heat at Kilmore but missed the semi-finals and is a smart pacer who has performed strongly in some good races at Melton this campaign, Stanley stablemate SOHO PARK AVENUE (9) was perhaps a bit plain in the semi but ran well from outside the leader in the first round of qualifiers and is a handy type, while Stewart’s LOWRIDER (11) and STAR VISION (6) are other contenders with the scratching of SOHO CHARMER (13). SELECTIONS: SOHO TRUMP (1), SEASIDE BOY (4), SOHO PARK AVENUE (9), LOWRIDER (11)

OVERVIEW: Wide open Vicbred Silver final for the three-year-old fillies where you can make a case for quite a few, but CYCLONE JENNI (2) looks well placed to run a good race from gate two. She settled last in the heat at Kilmore but flew late to grab fourth and then had no chance from a bad barrier in the semi-finals. Her win at Cranbourne before the Vicbred series was electric and she’s a handy type on the way up. TRYX VIXEN (1) very rarely finds the pegs in her races but I have some time for her and she can be a sharp improver from gate one, ISTHISTHEREALLIFE (6) led and was only nabbed late for second in a strong race at Cranbourne on Sunday and was very good in the same heat as CYCLONE JENNI (2), which was won by HEAVENLY FLYER (5), who has a sticky gate this time around. ALOT LIKE JEANNIE (9) won a Vicbred qualifier before being well held in the semis behind Bettor Beach, but is a chance here along with GINGER ELLA (3), MEZZANOTTI (4) and HEAVENLY FLYER (5). BACK: CYCLONE JENNI (2) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: CYCLONE JENNI (2), TRYX VIXEN (1), ISTHISTHEREALLIFE (6), ALOT LIKE JEANNIE (9)

OVERVIEW: SOHO PIASTRI (1) looks the one to beat here from the good draw. Michael Stanley’s charge never found the fence in his Vicbred heat at Kilmore and missed a place in the semi-finals, but had won in dominant fashion from the front at Newcastle before that. He’s a winner of four from 13 and deserves to be the favourite in this Vicbred Bronze clash. BLAZING HIGH (8) dropped out of his Vicbred heat after a tough trip but absolutely bolted in last time at Penrith and draws to trail the likely favourite here, MASON JOLIE (9) ran well for third at Cranbourne before a midfield finish in his heat of the Vicbred and looks a legitimate danger, while MASTER LOUEY (3) has placed a close-up second his past two at Cranbourne and has the ability to figure. SELECTIONS: SOHO PIASTRI (1), BLAZING HIGH (8), MASON JOLIE (9), MASTER LOUEY (3)

OVERVIEW: Not sure about the map in this clash, but I fancy ZANDA MAN (5) as a horse and think he has a bright future. He was caught parked in a strong race at Geelong last Friday but battled away to only be beaten 8.4m and I thought his first-up effort in a Vicbred heat from off the fence was good. He finished last campaign with a string of nice efforts, including a couple of Saturday night wins at Melton. Happy his way. BANJO STAR (9) raced roughly in his Vicbred heat, but his form over in Tasmania – including two wins and a tough second – is sound and he looks a promising type for Michael Breen, BINALONG MATE (1) sat parked for the last lap before only narrowly going down at Cranbourne on September 6 and has shown some good signs this preparation, while WARZONE (2) might have the speed to cross to the fence and from there would be a chance. He didn’t have much luck last time at Cranbourne when settling last, but his run before that was good and he won well leading at Ballarat on August 19. Other key runners include Sunday’s maiden winner KING BALDWIN (3), SOHO WASHINGTON (4) and HILLTONS SPIRIT (10). SELECTIONS: ZANDA MAN (5), BANJO STAR (9), BINALONG MATE (1), WARZONE (2)

OVERVIEW: Tricky race to line up with a few first-starters, but BAYSTYLE (2) is an experienced two-year-old with good gate speed who is already a three-time winner this season. He ran well when second to Group 1 Vicbred winner Some High in the heats of that series and was then caught parked and dropped out understandably in the semis. If he can get to the fence, he’s a key player. CASTERTON (6) has had the one trial for a close-up second placing at Ballarat, but there was no vision of that effort. He hails from the powerhouse Emma Stewart barn which produces young horses to win on debut time and time again, so monitor market expectations. LACE AND LEATHER (5) was part of a hot lead time and did a great job to sprint again and score on debut, while stablemate EDGAR BROMAC (3) came from well back in that same race to run third in an encouraging display. Others are worth considering, including DISPERSION (8) who is on debut after a couple of okay trials and NSW visitor PASSION AND PAIN (1), a three-time winner, from gate one. SELECTIONS: BAYSTYLE (2), CASTERTON (6), LACE AND LEATHER (5), EDGAR BROMAC (3)

OVERVIEW: MAJARO GIRL (10) bombed the start in the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series final for two-year-old trotting fillies last weekend but did a great job to finish sixth, albeit almost 35m from winner Kyvalley Dixon. She won a heat of the series prior to that and has improved nicely since joining the Andy Gath yard in June/July. She’s the youngest horse in this field, but there’s good scope there and she should give this a real shake. Fast-starter NIGHT FLIGHT (5) hasn’t raced for close to two months, but heads here on the back of two good runner-up placings and a nice trial win at Melton during the week, veteran BUSLIN BRODY (9) is always a chance in these types of races and must be respected at his best, while the lightly-raced ASPEN BELLE (6), who was outclassed in a Vicbred four-year-old trotting mares heat last time but has shown good signs this campaign, and the well-drawn SHES SKY HIGH (1) are contenders. BACK: MAJARO GIRL (10) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: MAJARO GIRL (10), NIGHT FLIGHT (5), BUSLIN BRODY (9), ASPEN BELLE (6)

OVERVIEW: BROADWAY OBSESSION (1) is first-up from a long break, but heads in on the back of a couple of good runner-up efforts at the Melton trials and draws to lead this assignment. Her first campaign reaped a win and second placing in a $20,000 Homegrown Classic, and there appears some good ability there. I like her chances. SOHO AMARYLLIS (3) won two races last preparation, made a late break first-up at Charlton and then just missed after a tough trip at Maryborough last time out. She’s got good ability, too. SWEET FLORABEL (7) was first past the post at Melton on August 28 but lost the race on protest, and while her manners are a cause for concern at this stage of her career, she looks to have a motor, while YOUVE BEEN SERVED (4) was disqualified after racing fiercely inside the pegs in her heat of the Vicbred series but has since trialled well at Maryborough. BACK: BROADWAY OBSESSION (1) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: BROADWAY OBSESSION (1), SOHO AMARYLLIS (3), SWEET FLORABEL (7), YOUVE BEEN SERVED (4)

OVERVIEW: DELS DESTINY (6) seems to always be running on late in his races without winning but strikes a small field and certainly appears to be going well enough to give this a real shake. He has raced in stronger grade for some time and been beaten less than 10m his last eight starts following a win in similar grade at Ballarat. He’s a safe trotter and it’s hard to see him not going close with the right trip. KENNYS SON (7) did everything right last time and won easily from the front, which followed two races where he made mistakes. It’s likely he will be driven aggressively, and from the front he would be very hard to catch. THATS MY CARDIGAN (5) is another of the gate speed runners who likes to race out in front and has won a couple of races in that role this campaign, while FLOATING MOUNTAIN (1) is certainly a winning chance given he hasn’t been far off the handy The Sky Is The Limit and Group 1 placegetter Hallebesofine in a couple of races in which he found the fence this preparation. SELECTIONS: DELS DESTINY (6), KENNYS SON (7), THATS MY CARDIGAN (5), FLOATING MOUNTAIN (1)

OVERVIEW: TWIGSTAR (2) was just so impressive when winning on debut at Cranbourne on September 6 that I have to be in her corner again here despite taking on the might of the Emma Stewart stable. In that first career run, the daughter of Poster Boy sat back last and rounded up her rivals three wide for the last lap in a solid 56.9 last half. That’s hard to do at Cranbourne and there’s a good wrap on her from trainer Scott Ewen. Stewart-trained runner FARADY (1) was close-up in a recent trial during mid-August (no vision), draws well and is raced by top owner-breeders Bruce and Vicki Edward. Monitor the market, but she will likely be short and this stable just churns out winners for fun. They look the two key winning chances, with LARACHA (5) and MY CRYSTAL VISION (4) showing enough in recent trials to suggest they can run well on debut. WHERES DAD (2) has gate speed and may be able to press forward and take up the lead in this race. She ran a good race last time out when able to drop onto the back of Tactique before running second to that horse. MCROCKIN (4) led before handing over to Feeling Happy last time out and finished in second in what was a solid effort. He has good gate speed and may look to find a prominent position again in this race. KIPCHOGE (3) has some early speed and should find a prominent position from a good draw in this race. He was forced to race without cover last time out at Marburg and was well beaten there. If he can find some cover this time he can look to bounce back. COLT KELLY (5) didn’t have a lot of luck last time out when checked in the run racing behind a runner which didn’t seem to handle the Redcliffe circuit. Having his third career start in this race he should be better for his first two outings. SELECTIONS: WHERES DAD (2), MCROCKIN (4), KIPCHOGE (3), COLT KELLY (5) SUGGESTED BET: WHERES DAD (2) to win.

FLORAS FOLLY (8) ran a good second last time out behind Usual Suspect at this track over the 1780. This looks a much easier race and she should get a good run off the speed which should see her running on strongly late. UNJUST ENRICHMENT (1) showed good gate speed initially last time out before handing over to Orion Art before being taken out of the race by that runner when it tired. He should get a good run from the ideal draw and can look to bounce back this time with a bit more luck in running. FRENCH BUBBLES (9) secured a good run last time out at Redcliffe and just couldn’t get into the race there which was taken out by Ideal Pursuit and dominated by runners close to the speed on the pegs. She finds a more suitable race and can be running into it late. LUVATINNY (6) got back in the run when on debut for the Dixon stable last time out before running through the line well enough in a race taken out by Notions. She is likely to have derived benefit from the outing and finds a weaker race. SELECTIONS: FLORAS FOLLY (8), UNJUST ENRICHMENT (1), FRENCH BUBBLES (9), LUVATINNY (6) SUGGESTED BET: FLORAS FOLLY (8) to win.

ITS ONE LIFE (7) isn’t a horse which possesses much gate speed which may see him shuffled back drawn inside the back row following out a horse with good gate speed. He put in a good run last time out after being shuffled back early in a race taken out by Mighty Ideal. EBONY BELLE (1) has good gate speed and seems to do her best work up on speed. She hasn’t been at her best recently but did put in a slightly better run last time out when finishing fourth behind Jilliby Panda at Marburg. THREE CHORD RIFF (9) set a strong tempo last time out in the final of the Showcase series behind Hes All Torque. She should secure a good run off the speed in this race and can be running on late. STONES (4) was forced to race without cover last time out and battled on well for third there behind Jilliby Panda at Marburg. He may be forced to do some again but finds a similar type of race. SELECTIONS: ITS ONE LIFE (7), EBONY BELLE (1), THREE CHORD RIFF (9), STONES (4) SUGGESTED BET: EBONY BELLE (1) to win.

ROYAL WINKLE (5) showed good gate speed last time out to lead but was shaded in the run by eventual winner Ultimate Hunter and just didn’t quite finish the race off. If he can find the front again and control things from there he should be hard to run down. TRACER BULLET (9) wasn’t beaten too far in fourth last time out in a similar type of race after sitting leaders back in the run. He should get a good run off the speed in this race and can look to be running on late into this race. TEACHERS PET (2) started a short priced favourite last time out at Marburg and never looked likely after not showing much gate speed early. If she can bounce somewhere nearer her best this would be a very suitable race. TACKAS LAST DANCE (4) secured a good run off the speed last time out and was running on late there into sixth in a race taken out by Sammys Secret. She is likely to get back again and can be running on late. SELECTIONS: ROYAL WINKLE (5), TRACER BULLET (9), TEACHERS PET (2), TACKAS LAST DANCE (4) SUGGESTED BET: ROYAL WINKLE (5) to win.

TAKE A CHANCE (9) put in a very good run last time out when finishing third behind Konnymara and Bonnies Cam who has since won. He draws to do no work early in this race and should be hard to beat in this type of grade. LAST CALL (5) was able to secure a good run off the speed last time out and was running on late in that race into third behind Digby Devil. She should get a good run off the speed in this race and will just be relying on the race being run to suit. DEEP REGRET (2) worked to the lead last time out before being run down late by One Chain Road who had the perfect run on his back. He draws well in this race and would likely be hard to run down if he was able to find the lead. MY SCIMITAR (10) did things wrong last time out and was taken out of play there as a result. He had been racing fairly leading into that run and with the race run to suit he could be running on late. SELECTIONS: TAKE A CHANCE (9), LAST CALL (5), DEEP REGRET (2), MY SCIMITAR (10) SUGGESTED BET: TAKE A CHANCE (9) to win.

LITTLELIONELJAMES (4) is a horse which seems to love racing over the short course and seemed to appreciate that step back in grade last time out when running into third there behind Francs For Coming. He draws well in this race and if he can find a prominent position he should run well. IAM HUGO (9) ran on well two starts ago at this track into third behind Magic Jujon and Stillyourshot in what was a stronger race. He is likely to get a good run off the speed in this race and should be running on strongly late. JIVE MASTER (7) draws awkwardly inside the back row in this race and will need luck at the right time. He drew poorly last time out before being shuffled back and was able to run on strongly there into second behind Francs For Coming. LITTLE SURFER GIRL (2) didn’t show much gate speed last time out which saw her crossed early and she just couldn’t quite go with the first few in a race the winner Favreau rated fast time of 1.57 for the 2040. SELECTIONS: LITTLELIONELJAMES (4), IAM HUGO (9), JIVE MASTER (7), LITTLE SURFER GIRL (2) SUGGESTED BET: IAM HUGO (9) each way.

CAPTAIN JAZZ (6) was a very impressive winner last time out when sitting without cover at this track and simply proving too good there holding them all off late. She draws poorly again but has shown she is a mare capable of working and looks hard to beat again. STILLYOURSHOT (1) has good gate speed and should be able to drive through and lead in this race before having options from there. He led at this track two starts ago and was just run down late there by Magic Jujon. WESTERN ARTERRA (7) should get a good run through in this race on the back of a horse with good gate speed. He secured a good run three starts ago and was running on well into second there behind Tilly Jayne. KIKI MEISTER (4) led last time out at Albion Park and ran a good third behind Dragon and Mach Assassin. He should settle close enough in this race from the front row draw and can look to be running on late. SELECTIONS: CAPTAIN JAZZ (6), STILLYOURSHOT (1), WESTERN ARTERRA (7), KIKI MEISTER (4) SUGGESTED BET:

ITS BACK PAGE NEWS (3) has good gate speed and should be able to find a prominent position in this race from a good draw. She led five starts ago at this track and distance and can look to do the same again in this race. HARRY KANE (7) trialled up reasonably in a strong trial taken out by Captain Shuffles recently at Albion Park. He draws awkwardly inside the back row but is seemingly a horse that does his best work when sat up and saved for one run. MISTER DELWIN (9) was forced to race without cover last time out at this track when finishing second to Digby Devil. He should get a good run off the speed early and has options from there whether he then looks to work around to the breeze again. HOLME BOY (4) scored a huge win last time out at Marburg when getting back in the run before finishing over the top late to score. He should get a good run off the speed again in this race and can be running on late. SELECTIONS: ITS BACK PAGE NEWS (3), HARRY KANE (7), MISTER DELWIN (9), HOLME BOY (4) SUGGESTED BET: ITS BACK PAGE NEWS (3) to win.

COSMIC FLYER (6) secured a good run last race start when finishing fifth behind Dragon at Albion Park. He has since trialled and won at Marburg in reasonable time. He should be running on strongly. STORMTIDE (1) was badly held up at this track two starts ago before eventually getting into the clear and flashing into second behind Merry Jewel. He should have the speed to lead initially in this race before having options from there. MAHINDI (5) got back in the run last time out and was running on well there into fourth behind Sporty Zara at this track. She is likely to be shuffled back again in this race and can be running on late. MY ULTIMATE CARTER (7) looked to be very unlucky last time out when travelling nicely looking for a run which never came. He should get a good run through in the early stages and will just be relying on luck at the right time to get into the clear. SELECTIONS: COSMIC FLYER (6), STORMTIDE (1), MAHINDI (5), MY ULTIMATE CARTER (7) SUGGESTED BET: STORMTIDE (1) to win.
